title: Kissed Buttery Chinese Cox Apple Wonton Soup
description: A buttery and tender Yunnan-inspired dish featuring Cox apples, served in a wonton soup, perfect for a brunch mood. This Jain-friendly recipe is a unique twist on traditional Chinese cuisine.
instructions: In a large pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat and add the grated ginger, cooking until fragrant.
Add the diced Cox apples to the pan and cook until they are tender, about 5 minutes.
Deglaze the pan with a small amount of vegetable broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
In a separate pot, bring the remaining vegetable broth to a boil and then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Assemble the wontons by placing a small spoonful of the cooked apple mixture onto the center of a wonton wrapper, and then brushing the edges with sesame oil and folding the wrapper into a triangle.
Add the wontons to the simmering broth and cook for 2-3 minutes, or until they float to the surface.
Season the broth with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve the wonton soup hot, garnished with chopped green onions and a pat of butter on top.
Drizzle the remaining 2 tablespoons of melted butter over the top of the soup and serve immediately.
